    <bpmn:task id="Task_OrderSeveralShops" name="Order parts from several shops (cheapest parts)"/>

    <bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent id="Event_PartsBatchArrived" name="Parts batch arrived">
      <bpmn:messageEventDefinition id="MED_PartsBatchArrived" messageRef="Message_PartsBatch"/>
    </bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_BuildWithParts" name="Start or continue building with arrived parts"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_CheckStock" name="Check stock level of each part"/>
    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_StockLevel" name="Stock level of a single part?" default="Flow_StockOk"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_ReorderFastest" name="Reorder part (fastest parts)"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_ReorderCheapest" name="Reorder part (cheapest parts)"/>
    <bpmn:task id="Task_WriteComplaintMail" name="Write mail to friends complaining about web shops"/>
    <bpmn:endEvent id="End_ComplaintSent" name="Complaint mail sent"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_01" sourceRef="Start_Needed" targetRef="Task_QueryShops"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_02" sourceRef="Task_QueryShops" targetRef="Task_CompareOffers"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_03" sourceRef="Task_CompareOffers" targetRef="Task_CreateOrderList"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_04" sourceRef="Task_CreateOrderList" targetRef="Gateway_OneShopSufficient"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_OneShopYes" sourceRef="Gateway_OneShopSufficient" targetRef="Task_OrderOneShop">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">${oneShopSufficient == true}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_OneShopNo" sourceRef="Gateway_OneShopSufficient" targetRef="Task_OrderSeveralShops"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_07" sourceRef="Task_OrderOneShop" targetRef="Gateway_OrdersJoin"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_08" sourceRef="Task_OrderSeveralShops" targetRef="Gateway_OrdersJoin"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_09" sourceRef="Gateway_OrdersJoin" targetRef="Gateway_PartsMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_10" sourceRef="Gateway_PartsMerge" targetRef="Event_PartsBatchArrived"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_11" sourceRef="Event_PartsBatchArrived" targetRef="Task_BuildWithParts"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_12" sourceRef="Task_BuildWithParts" targetRef="Task_CheckStock"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_13" sourceRef="Task_CheckStock" targetRef="Gateway_StockLevel"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_StockZero" sourceRef="Gateway_StockLevel" targetRef="Task_WriteComplaintMail">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">${stockLevelOfPart == 0}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_StockBelow3" sourceRef="Gateway_StockLevel" targetRef="Task_ReorderFastest">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">${stockLevelOfPart > 0 && stockLevelOfPart < 3}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_StockBelow5" sourceRef="Gateway_StockLevel" targetRef="Task_ReorderCheapest">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">${stockLevelOfPart >= 3 && stockLevelOfPart < 5}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_StockOk" sourceRef="Gateway_StockLevel" targetRef="Gateway_PartsMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_ReorderFastestDone" sourceRef="Task_ReorderFastest" targetRef="Gateway_PartsMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_ReorderCheapestDone" sourceRef="Task_ReorderCheapest" targetRef="Gateway_PartsMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_MailSent" sourceRef="Task_WriteComplaintMail" targetRef="End_ComplaintSent"/>
  </bpmn:process>

rules.instruction: When the description asks for a BPMN process model to be delivered as BPMN XML, so the output must include a diagram section: When a BPMN model is delivered as XML, always include a bpmndi:BPMNDiagram element as the diagram section of bpmn:definitions, and give it exactly one bpmndi:BPMNPlane child whose bpmnElement references the process or collaboration being shown. Without this child the XML fails schema validation, even when the process elements themselves are correct.
rules.situation: the description asks for a BPMN process model to be delivered as BPMN XML, so the output must include a diagram section

rules.instruction: When the description compares one measured value of an item against several thresholds, and each range between thresholds triggers a different action, including a range at the lowest value: Model one exclusive gateway directly after the measurement activity. Give each stated range its own outgoing sequence flow, labeled with that range. Lead each flow to the action the description assigns to that range, including the range at the lowest value, which gets its own branch. Do not drop a range, and do not replace the gateway with an unconditional flow or with separate unrelated checks.
rules.situation: the description compares one measured value of an item against several thresholds, and each range between thresholds triggers a different action, including a range at the lowest value

rules.instruction: When the description says physical goods from an outside source arrive, and the participant then starts working with the arrived goods; the arrival is something the participant takes in, not a notification, timer, or condition: Model the receipt of the physical goods as a manual task performed by that participant, placed in the sequence before the activity that works with the goods. Do not model the arrival as an intermediate catch event. Reserve intermediate catch events for waits on messages, signals, timers, or conditions.
rules.situation: the description says physical goods from an outside source arrive, and the participant then starts working with the arrived goods; the arrival is something the participant takes in, not a notification, timer, or condition

rules.instruction: When the description says that several activities or item branches start at the same time after one point, and that a following step begins once the first of the concurrently arriving items is available, while the remaining items keep arriving in an unspecified order and must not hold up that step: Open the concurrent activities and item branches with a parallel gateway split placed before them, with one outgoing flow per branch and no conditions on those flows. Model the junction before the first-arrival step as a complex gateway that continues on the first incoming token, not as a parallel join that waits for every branch. Keep the handling of the remaining arrivals on their own branches, linked to the process so they do not block the continuation.
rules.situation: the description says that several activities or item branches start at the same time after one point, and that a following step begins once the first of the concurrently arriving items is available, while the remaining items keep arriving in an unspecified order and must not hold up that step

rules.instruction: When the description monitors several items (for example, the stock of each part) against a limit, and a stated decision on whether any item has crossed a limit comes before the item-by-item checks that determine which item it was and which follow-up applies: Model an outer exclusive gateway that tests whether any monitored item has crossed a limit, placed before the item-specific comparisons. Its branch for 'none crossed' goes directly to the step after the checks, and its branch for 'at least one crossed' leads into the item-specific gateway chain. Do not start with the item-specific comparison alone when the description first asks the general question. Keep the item-specific comparisons and their follow-up tasks as described, and rejoin all branches before the next step.

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity begins when the first of several arriving items has been received, and that the same activity then continues while the remaining items arrive: Model the start of the activity as its own task, placed after the event or gateway that signals the first arrival. Model the continuing work as a separate task on the flow that follows, so that the arrival event does not lead directly to the next decision. Do not omit either task, and do not replace the ongoing work with an unconditional flow to the next step.
